validity.researcher_notes: Sheet LengthKnown=9.00 mi does not match any independent source found. WBUR (Miriam Wasser, 2022-12-15, wbur.org) states the project is 'a new 5.3 mile underground gas pipeline'; the official EFSB/DPU Notice of Adjudication and Public Comment Hearing (docket EFSB 22-05/D.P.U. 22-69, hosted by the City of Springfield) states verbatim 'installation of approximately 5.3 miles of new 16-inch pipeline'; EIA's own Aug2026 release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', row 135) also now shows Miles=5.3, having corrected its own historical figure starting with a mid-2020s release. Traced GEM's 9.00/EIA long-format history (sources/eia_pipeline_projects/data/eia_projects_long.csv, 2022-01..2026-08 releases): every EIA release through 2025-07 carried Miles=9.0, matching GEM's sheet value exactly -- strong circumstantial evidence GEM's row was populated from an early/stale EIA snapshot and never refreshed even after EIA itself corrected the figure. 5.3 mi is corroborated by 2 independent origins (WBUR journalism + the government-hosted EFSB/DPU notice) plus EIA's own corrected current release -- high tier.

Independent cost reporting shows real escalation over time: WBUR (2022-12-15) states 'the $65 million proposal from Eversource'; Eversource's own current project page (fetched 2026-09-14) states 'The estimated project cost is $85 million, based on the current cost of materials, equipment and labor... those costs can change over time.' Neither GEM's $33M nor EIA's $33M matches the project's cost at ANY point in its documented history (2022: $65M: 2026: $85M) -- the $33M figure appears to be a stale/erroneous carry that predates the earliest evidence I could find. $85M is single-source (Eversource's own current page) for the CURRENT figure specifically; WBUR's $65M is a different point in time (2022), showing the escalation trend rather than corroborating $85M directly. Searched for a second 2025/2026 source stating $85M specifically (Daily Hampshire Gazette/gazettenet.com and a June-2026 thereminder.com follow-up were both located earlier in this research session but could not be re-verified through url_verifier before this session's web-search budget was exhausted) -- flagging as medium tier pending that second confirmation.

validity.recommendation: verify Start/End directionality -- the physical origin (new TGP interconnect/point-of-delivery station) is in Longmeadow, MA and the terminus (Bliss Street Regulator Station) is in Springfield, MA; the sheet currently records Start=Springfield / End=Longmeadow, which appears reversed
validity.researcher_notes: Both cities (Springfield, Longmeadow, MA) are correctly identified as the project's two endpoints -- no error there. But the official EFSB/DPU notice describes the flow of construction/gas explicitly: '...installation of a new delivery point (POD) adjacent to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company (TGP) meter station to be constructed in LONGMEADOW; installation of approximately 5.3 miles of new 16-inch pipeline... in Longmeadow and Springfield; and upgrades at the existing Bliss Street Regulator Station [in SPRINGFIELD] to connect the Project to the existing distribution system.' EIA's own notes field (Aug2026 release, row 135) describes it the same way: 'connecting a new TGP meter/point-of-delivery station in Longmeadow to Eversource's Bliss Street Regulator Station [in Springfield].' This is a single origin (the petition, restated in both the EFSB notice and EIA's derived notes) but internally consistent and unambiguous about directionality -- flagging as a directional swap to verify/correct, not asserting it as a hard, independently double-sourced fact.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The EIA pre-matched candidate comparison for this row flags Status: sheet 'proposed' vs EIA 'On Hold' (~= GEM's 'shelved') as DIFFERS. I evaluated this directly rather than passing it through. Weighing the evidence: (1) Eversource's own live current page (the operator/petitioner itself, and the freshest single source available) still labels the project 'Proposed' and describes active regulatory review, not withdrawal or suspension; (2) a 2025-08-07/08-12 public listening session (Eversource's own page + independent thereminder.com coverage) shows continued public engagement well within the last ~13 months; (3) the EFSB/DPU docket (opened 2022, notice period ongoing) has not been closed or dismissed in anything I found. GEM's dormancy rule is 'no development updates for >=2 years post-proposal -> shelved'; the most recent confirmed activity (Aug 2025 forum) is ~13 months before this review (Sept 2026), well under that 2-year threshold, so the shelved trigger is NOT met. EIA's internal 'On Hold' tag is a real, independently-maintained data point (their own dataset, not derived from GEM) and is worth flagging/monitoring -- it may reflect EIA's read on the stalled MEPA/SDEIR timeline -- but is not enough on its own to override the operator's own current self-description plus documented 2025 activity. Verdict: confirm (Status stays 'proposed'; Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed already correctly capture the real-world delay). Recommend re-checking in ~12 months: if no SDEIR is filed and no further public activity is found by roughly 2027-08 (2 years past the last confirmed 2025-08 activity), the shelved threshold would then be met.

summary: Real, singular, correctly-attributed proposed-status gas pipeline project (Eversource, Springfield-Longmeadow MA); GEM's LengthKnown (9.0mi) and SegmentCost ($33M) are stale figures traced to an early/never-refreshed EIA snapshot -- corrected to 5.3mi (high tier, 3 sources) and ~$85M (medium tier, single current source) with spec concerns staged; a Start/End directionality attribution concern also staged. Status confirmed as 'proposed' (not changed to shelved) after reconciling against EIA's own 'On Hold' tag -- GEM's 2-year dormancy threshold is not met (most recent confirmed activity Aug 2025). PipelineType, ConstructionYear, StartYear1, Capacity, and FuelSource left UNRESOLVED -- no source found for any of them.
